DEF-V001-2025-001.description: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump showing abnormal pressure fluctuations during operation. Fuel delivery pressure dropping intermittently from 350 bar to 280 bar causing engine power reduction. Suspect worn plunger barrel assembly and delivery valve requiring replacement.
DEF-V001-2025-001.descriptionHtml: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump showing abnormal pressure fluctuations during operation. Fuel delivery pressure dropping intermittently from 350 bar to 280 bar causing engine power reduction. Suspect worn plunger barrel assembly and delivery valve requiring replacement.
DEF-V001-2025-001.descriptionText: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump showing abnormal pressure fluctuations during operation. Fuel delivery pressure dropping intermittently from 350 bar to 280 bar causing engine power reduction. Suspect worn plunger barrel assembly and delivery valve requiring replacement.
DEF-V001-2025-001.actionTakenRequested: Replace fuel injection pump plunger and barrel assembly. Overhaul delivery valve. Conduct fuel pressure test after repair.
DEF-V001-2025-001.immediateCauseExplanation: Fuel injection pump has exceeded recommended overhaul interval of 12,000 running hours. Current RH is 14,500. Normal wear pattern accelerated by high sulfur fuel usage in certain trading areas.
DEF-V001-2025-001.rootCauseExplanation: PMS maintenance interval was not updated when fuel quality parameters changed. Spare parts order was delayed due to budget constraints in Q3.
DEF-V001-2025-001.closureComment: Fuel injection pump overhauled successfully. New plunger and barrel assembly fitted. Delivery valve replaced. Fuel pressure test conducted - all parameters normal. Engine load test completed satisfactorily.

notes.noteText: Spare parts received from MAN B&W Singapore branch
Overhaul completed in 6 hours with maker's representative supervision

actions.actionDescription: Replace fuel injection pump plunger barrel assembly and delivery valve
Update PMS maintenance interval for all fuel injection pumps to 10,000 RH

DEF-V001-2025-002.description: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump - Recurring issue. Fuel pressure again dropping below normal operating parameters. After previous repair in October, pump functioned normally for 40 days before symptoms reappeared. Suspect defective replacement parts or underlying system issue.
DEF-V001-2025-002.descriptionHtml: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump - Recurring issue. Fuel pressure again dropping below normal operating parameters. After previous repair in October, pump functioned normally for 40 days before symptoms reappeared. Suspect defective replacement parts or underlying system issue.
DEF-V001-2025-002.descriptionText: Main Engine No.1 Fuel Injection Pump - Recurring issue. Fuel pressure again dropping below normal operating parameters. After previous repair in October, pump functioned normally for 40 days before symptoms reappeared. Suspect defective replacement parts or underlying system issue.
DEF-V001-2025-002.actionTakenRequested: Conduct comprehensive fuel system analysis. Check fuel quality. Inspect all related components including fuel lines, filters, and fuel oil heaters.
DEF-V001-2025-002.immediateCauseExplanation: Replacement parts from October repair may have been substandard or fuel system contamination causing accelerated wear.

systemFactor: Spare parts quality verification process inadequate

DEF-V001-2025-002.rootCauseExplanation: Parts sourced from third-party supplier without OEM certification. Fuel testing only done at bunkering, not regular intervals.

notes.noteText: Fuel sample sent for laboratory analysis. Results expected in 5 days.
Technical superintendent consulted. Recommended complete fuel system inspection.

actions.actionDescription: Send fuel samples for comprehensive laboratory analysis
Arrange maker's representative to inspect complete fuel injection system at next port
Review and update spare parts procurement policy to require OEM certification

DEF-V001-2025-003.description: Emergency Generator failed to start automatically during weekly test. Manual start successful but auto-start relay found defective. Class surveyor present during annual survey identified this as Condition of Class item requiring rectification within 3 months.
DEF-V001-2025-003.descriptionHtml: Emergency Generator failed to start automatically during weekly test. Manual start successful but auto-start relay found defective. Class surveyor present during annual survey identified this as Condition of Class item requiring rectification within 3 months.
DEF-V001-2025-003.descriptionText: Emergency Generator failed to start automatically during weekly test. Manual start successful but auto-start relay found defective. Class surveyor present during annual survey identified this as Condition of Class item requiring rectification within 3 months.
DEF-V001-2025-003.actionTakenRequested: Replace auto-start relay. Conduct full function test of emergency generator including blackout simulation. Present to Class surveyor for CoC lift.
DEF-V001-2025-003.immediateCauseExplanation: Auto-start relay is original equipment from 2018. Contact resistance increased beyond acceptable limits causing intermittent starting failure.

systemFactor: No planned replacement schedule for relays
Condition monitoring not implemented for starting circuit

DEF-V001-2025-003.rootCauseExplanation: Electrical components like relays not included in regular PMS schedule. Only visual inspection performed, no electrical testing of contact resistance.

notes.noteText: Class surveyor imposed CoC with 3-month deadline. Copy of survey report received.
Replacement relay ordered from Caterpillar authorized dealer in Singapore. ETA: 2 weeks.
Flag state notified as per regulation requirements.

actions.actionDescription: Procure and replace auto-start relay with OEM part
Conduct blackout simulation test after relay replacement
Arrange Class surveyor attendance for CoC closure
Add all emergency generator electrical components to PMS with 5-year replacement cycle

DEF-V001-2025-004.description: Port side lifeboat davit wire showing visible broken strands exceeding 10% in one lay length. Identified during PSC inspection at Houston. Condition of Class imposed by attending Class surveyor. Wire replacement mandatory before next port departure.
DEF-V001-2025-004.descriptionHtml: Port side lifeboat davit wire showing visible broken strands exceeding 10% in one lay length. Identified during PSC inspection at Houston. Condition of Class imposed by attending Class surveyor. Wire replacement mandatory before next port departure.
DEF-V001-2025-004.descriptionText: Port side lifeboat davit wire showing visible broken strands exceeding 10% in one lay length. Identified during PSC inspection at Houston. Condition of Class imposed by attending Class surveyor. Wire replacement mandatory before next port departure.
DEF-V001-2025-004.actionTakenRequested: Replace lifeboat davit wire. Conduct load test. Present to Class surveyor for CoC lift before departure.
DEF-V001-2025-004.immediateCauseExplanation: Davit wire exposed to high stress during regular drills combined with salt spray corrosion accelerated strand breakage.

individualFactor: Inspection not thorough during weekly checks
systemFactor: Wire rope inspection criteria not clear in checklist

DEF-V001-2025-004.rootCauseExplanation: Weekly davit inspection checklist did not specify detailed wire examination requirements. Crew training on wire rope rejection criteria needed.
DEF-V001-2025-004.closureComment: New davit wire installed. Load test conducted with 1.1 times Safe Working Load. Class surveyor attended and lifted CoC. PSC deficiency rectified. Departure clearance obtained.

notes.noteText: Emergency wire procurement arranged from local Vestdavit agent in Houston.
Wire delivered to vessel. Replacement work started.
Class surveyor from DNV attended. CoC lifted. PSC release obtained.

actions.actionDescription: Procure and install new davit wire - emergency basis
Conduct load test with Class surveyor witness
Revise weekly lifeboat inspection checklist to include detailed wire examination criteria
Fleet-wide training on wire rope inspection and rejection criteria

DEF-V001-2025-005.description: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal leaking heavily. Pump taken out of service. Ballast operations can continue with No.1 pump but redundancy compromised. Mechanical seal kit ordered.
DEF-V001-2025-005.descriptionHtml: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal leaking heavily. Pump taken out of service. Ballast operations can continue with No.1 pump but redundancy compromised. Mechanical seal kit ordered.
DEF-V001-2025-005.descriptionText: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal leaking heavily. Pump taken out of service. Ballast operations can continue with No.1 pump but redundancy compromised. Mechanical seal kit ordered.
DEF-V001-2025-005.actionTakenRequested: Replace mechanical seal. Test pump operation. Return to service.

unsafeCondition: Seal wear due to abrasive particles in ballast water

DEF-V001-2025-005.immediateCauseExplanation: Ballast water strainer mesh size may be allowing fine particles to reach the pump, causing premature seal wear.
DEF-V001-2025-005.rootCauseExplanation: Strainer mesh may be too coarse for current trading pattern. More fine sediment in coastal waters than anticipated.

notes.noteText: Seal kit ordered from Wartsila Singapore. Expected delivery at next port call (Singapore).

actions.actionDescription: Replace mechanical seal upon parts arrival
Review and upgrade ballast strainer mesh size

DEF-V001-2025-006.description: S-Band Radar (Radar No.2) displaying intermittent video freeze on screen. Issue occurs approximately every 30 minutes and lasts for 2-3 seconds. Vessel still has full navigation capability with X-Band radar operational. Service engineer visit requested.
DEF-V001-2025-006.descriptionHtml: S-Band Radar (Radar No.2) displaying intermittent video freeze on screen. Issue occurs approximately every 30 minutes and lasts for 2-3 seconds. Vessel still has full navigation capability with X-Band radar operational. Service engineer visit requested.
DEF-V001-2025-006.descriptionText: S-Band Radar (Radar No.2) displaying intermittent video freeze on screen. Issue occurs approximately every 30 minutes and lasts for 2-3 seconds. Vessel still has full navigation capability with X-Band radar operational. Service engineer visit requested.
DEF-V001-2025-006.actionTakenRequested: Arrange Kongsberg service engineer to inspect and repair at next suitable port.
DEF-V001-2025-006.immediateCauseExplanation: Video freeze pattern suggests display processor or graphics card intermittent failure. Antenna rotation normal.

systemFactor: Equipment approaching end of service life

DEF-V001-2025-006.rootCauseExplanation: Radar system installed in 2019 approaching 6 years of continuous operation. Some components may need proactive replacement.

notes.noteText: Contacted Kongsberg service center. Engineer availability confirmed for Rotterdam port call on Dec 15-16.

actions.actionDescription: Arrange Kongsberg service engineer attendance at Rotterdam

DEF-V001-2025-007.description: Sewage Treatment Plant UV sterilization unit showing reduced effectiveness. Effluent coliform count slightly elevated but still within MARPOL limits. UV lamp replacement recommended during next dry dock.
DEF-V001-2025-007.descriptionHtml: Sewage Treatment Plant UV sterilization unit showing reduced effectiveness. Effluent coliform count slightly elevated but still within MARPOL limits. UV lamp replacement recommended during next dry dock.
DEF-V001-2025-007.descriptionText: Sewage Treatment Plant UV sterilization unit showing reduced effectiveness. Effluent coliform count slightly elevated but still within MARPOL limits. UV lamp replacement recommended during next dry dock.
DEF-V001-2025-007.actionTakenRequested: Monitor effluent quality weekly. Replace UV lamps during scheduled dry dock in Q1 2026.
DEF-V001-2025-007.defectCategory: Environmental / Pollution Control (e.g., BWM, SOx, OWS)
DEF-V001-2025-007.immediateCauseExplanation: UV lamps have exceeded recommended operating hours. Output reduced but still functional.

systemFactor: Replacement schedule aligned with dry dock - acceptable delay

DEF-V001-2025-007.rootCauseExplanation: UV lamp replacement is a planned maintenance item. Current degradation within acceptable limits until dry dock.
DEF-V001-2025-007.deferReason: Effluent still within MARPOL compliance limits. UV lamp replacement scheduled for Q1 2026 dry dock.

notes.noteText: Weekly effluent testing shows coliform count at 180/100ml (limit is 250/100ml). Within acceptable range.
Deferment approved by Technical Superintendent. UV lamps included in dry dock work scope.

actions.actionDescription: Replace UV lamps during Q1 2026 dry dock
Continue weekly effluent testing and record results

DEF-V001-2025-008.description: Fire detection panel Zone 4 (Accommodation Deck 3) showing intermittent Earth Fault alarm. All smoke detectors in zone tested and found operational. Suspected cable insulation degradation. Cable tracing and repair completed.
DEF-V001-2025-008.descriptionHtml: Fire detection panel Zone 4 (Accommodation Deck 3) showing intermittent Earth Fault alarm. All smoke detectors in zone tested and found operational. Suspected cable insulation degradation. Cable tracing and repair completed.
DEF-V001-2025-008.descriptionText: Fire detection panel Zone 4 (Accommodation Deck 3) showing intermittent Earth Fault alarm. All smoke detectors in zone tested and found operational. Suspected cable insulation degradation. Cable tracing and repair completed.
DEF-V001-2025-008.actionTakenRequested: Trace detection loop cable. Identify and repair insulation damage.
DEF-V001-2025-008.immediateCauseExplanation: Detection loop cable passing through bulkhead penetration was chafing against the gland, causing intermittent earth fault.

systemFactor: Bulkhead penetration gland not properly fitted during installation

DEF-V001-2025-008.rootCauseExplanation: Original installation may have had insufficient cable protection at penetration point. Added cable sleeve for protection.
DEF-V001-2025-008.closureComment: Cable traced through Zone 4 accommodation deck. Found chafing damage at frame 45 bulkhead penetration. Damaged section cut out and cable re-terminated. Cable sleeve fitted for protection. Full zone test conducted - no earth faults. System returned to normal.

notes.noteText: Megger test on detection loop showed 2 Megohm (should be >10 Megohm). Earth fault confirmed.
Cable damage located at bulkhead penetration frame 45. Approximately 50mm of cable affected.

actions.actionDescription: Trace detection loop cable and locate earth fault
Repair cable insulation damage and re-terminate
Inspect all bulkhead cable penetrations in fire detection system

DEF-V001-2025-009.description: Steering gear hydraulic oil temperature running higher than normal. Operating at 55°C (normal is 40-45°C). No visible leaks. Hydraulic oil cooler effectiveness reduced. Cooler cleaning scheduled.
DEF-V001-2025-009.descriptionHtml: Steering gear hydraulic oil temperature running higher than normal. Operating at 55°C (normal is 40-45°C). No visible leaks. Hydraulic oil cooler effectiveness reduced. Cooler cleaning scheduled.
DEF-V001-2025-009.descriptionText: Steering gear hydraulic oil temperature running higher than normal. Operating at 55°C (normal is 40-45°C). No visible leaks. Hydraulic oil cooler effectiveness reduced. Cooler cleaning scheduled.
DEF-V001-2025-009.actionTakenRequested: Clean hydraulic oil cooler. Check cooler tube bundle for blockage or scaling. Verify seawater flow.

unsafeCondition: Cooler tube fouling from marine growth

DEF-V001-2025-009.immediateCauseExplanation: Extended operation in warm tropical waters has accelerated marine growth inside cooler tubes on seawater side.

systemFactor: Cooler cleaning interval may need shortening for tropical trading

DEF-V001-2025-009.rootCauseExplanation: Current 6-month cooler cleaning interval may be insufficient for continuous tropical operation. Consider 3-month interval.

notes.noteText: Monitoring oil temperature closely. Alarm limit is 65°C. Currently stable at 55°C.

actions.actionDescription: Clean hydraulic oil cooler seawater side at next port
Review and update cooler cleaning interval in PMS for tropical trading

DEF-V001-2025-010.description: Forward mooring winch No.1 brake band showing excessive wear. Brake lining thickness reduced to 4mm (minimum is 3mm). Brake still functional but replacement parts ordered for precautionary maintenance.
DEF-V001-2025-010.descriptionHtml: Forward mooring winch No.1 brake band showing excessive wear. Brake lining thickness reduced to 4mm (minimum is 3mm). Brake still functional but replacement parts ordered for precautionary maintenance.
DEF-V001-2025-010.descriptionText: Forward mooring winch No.1 brake band showing excessive wear. Brake lining thickness reduced to 4mm (minimum is 3mm). Brake still functional but replacement parts ordered for precautionary maintenance.
DEF-V001-2025-010.actionTakenRequested: Order brake band replacement parts. Replace brake band before next major port operation.

unsafeCondition: Normal wear from frequent mooring operations

DEF-V001-2025-010.immediateCauseExplanation: Vessel has completed 45 port calls this year with multiple mooring operations per call. High usage causing accelerated wear.

systemFactor: High trading frequency impact on equipment wear rates

DEF-V001-2025-010.rootCauseExplanation: Current liner trades require frequent port calls. May need to stock additional spare brake bands onboard.

notes.noteText: Brake band spare parts ordered from local supplier. Expected delivery in 3 days.
Bosun team prepared tools and equipment for brake band replacement.

actions.actionDescription: Procure replacement brake band and lining
Replace brake band upon parts arrival
Increase spare brake band stock level to 2 sets per winch

systemFactor: Inadequate Stock control / Spare parts inventory control

actions.actionDescription: sd

DEF-V001-2025-013.description: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal failure - RECURRING ISSUE. Seal replaced in December 2025, now leaking again after only 30 days service. Symptoms identical to previous failure. Suggests underlying root cause not addressed - strainer upgrade was not completed.
DEF-V001-2025-013.descriptionHtml: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal failure - RECURRING ISSUE. Seal replaced in December 2025, now leaking again after only 30 days service. Symptoms identical to previous failure. Suggests underlying root cause not addressed - strainer upgrade was not completed.
DEF-V001-2025-013.descriptionText: No.2 Ballast Pump mechanical seal failure - RECURRING ISSUE. Seal replaced in December 2025, now leaking again after only 30 days service. Symptoms identical to previous failure. Suggests underlying root cause not addressed - strainer upgrade was not completed.
DEF-V001-2025-013.actionTakenRequested: Replace mechanical seal again. Complete strainer mesh upgrade as mandatory preventive action. Investigate root cause of premature seal failure.

unsafeCondition: Seal wear due to abrasive particles in ballast water
Strainer mesh upgrade not completed as previously recommended

DEF-V001-2025-013.immediateCauseExplanation: Strainer upgrade recommended in previous defect was not completed due to parts availability. Abrasive particles continue to damage the seal.

individualFactor: Previous preventive action not followed through
systemFactor: Preventive action tracking system not enforced

DEF-V001-2025-013.rootCauseExplanation: Root cause analysis reveals that the strainer upgrade recommended in DEF-V001-2025-005 was not completed. This is a systemic failure in preventive action follow-up and parts procurement escalation.

notes.noteText: This is a recurring failure - same equipment, same failure mode as DEF-V001-2025-005 from November 2025. Escalated to Fleet Manager for review.
Fleet Manager confirmed: strainer upgrade now mandatory. Parts expedited from Rotterdam.

actions.actionDescription: Replace mechanical seal with upgraded high-grade silicon carbide seal
Install upgraded 100-micron strainer mesh (MANDATORY)
Implement ballast water sediment sampling protocol

DEF-V001-2025-014.description: Steering gear hydraulic oil high temperature alarm activated - RECURRING ISSUE. Temperature now reaching 62°C despite cooler cleaning performed in November 2025. Alarm set point is 60°C. Normal operating temp 40-45°C. Steering functionality unaffected but thermal stress on components increasing.
DEF-V001-2025-014.descriptionHtml: Steering gear hydraulic oil high temperature alarm activated - RECURRING ISSUE. Temperature now reaching 62°C despite cooler cleaning performed in November 2025. Alarm set point is 60°C. Normal operating temp 40-45°C. Steering functionality unaffected but thermal stress on components increasing.
DEF-V001-2025-014.descriptionText: Steering gear hydraulic oil high temperature alarm activated - RECURRING ISSUE. Temperature now reaching 62°C despite cooler cleaning performed in November 2025. Alarm set point is 60°C. Normal operating temp 40-45°C. Steering functionality unaffected but thermal stress on components increasing.
DEF-V001-2025-014.actionTakenRequested: Replace hydraulic oil cooler completely. Conduct hydraulic oil analysis. Check relief valve settings and pump efficiency.

unsafeCondition: Cooler tube scaling beyond surface cleaning capability
Hydraulic oil degradation affecting heat transfer

DEF-V001-2025-014.immediateCauseExplanation: Previous cleaning addressed external fouling but internal tube scaling remains. Hydraulic oil analysis pending to confirm oil condition.

systemFactor: Cooler maintenance interval may be insufficient for current operating profile
Internal scaling not addressed during routine cleaning

DEF-V001-2025-014.rootCauseExplanation: The previous maintenance only addressed external fouling. Internal tube scaling requires chemical cleaning or replacement which was not performed. The cooler is approaching end of service life.

notes.noteText: This is a recurrence of high temp issue from November 2025. Previous cleaning did not resolve the root cause. Cooler replacement now mandatory.
New cooler ordered from Rolls-Royce Singapore. Lead time 3 weeks. Meanwhile monitoring temp closely and reducing hydraulic pump output slightly.
Hydraulic oil sample sent to lab in Singapore. Results expected in 5 days.

actions.actionDescription: Replace hydraulic oil cooler with new unit
Conduct hydraulic oil analysis to check for degradation
Update PMS to include annual chemical cleaning of cooler internals
4-hourly temperature logging until cooler replacement
